column5: Case study anchor

column4: Medical Secretaries may check whether a referral is complete and request missing information, but must not assess clinical suitability or decide whether the referral should be accepted.
column5: "Medical Secretaries may identify missing information... not permitted to assess clinical suitability"

column4: Once completeness checks are finished, the referral must be passed to the appropriate Consultant for clinical review.
column5: "referral is passed to the appropriate Consultant for clinical review"

column4: The Consultant's decision (accept / reject / request further information / redirect) must be recorded together with the reason for the decision and the identity of the person making it.
column5: "The reason for the decision and the identity of the person making it must be recorded"

column4: A New Patient Appointment may only be arranged after an authorised Consultant has accepted the referral.
column5: "A New Patient Appointment may only be arranged after an authorised Consultant has accepted the referral"

column4: A Treatment Booking Request that has not been completed and authorised by an appropriate clinical professional must not be processed by administrative staff.
column5: "A request that has not been completed and authorised... must not be processed by administrative staff"

column4: Decisions on whether treatment should continue, be delayed or be changed following an inter-cycle clinical review are clinical decisions only; they cannot be made by the Treatment Bookings Team, the Finance Team or any other administrative employee.
column5: "These are clinical decisions and cannot be made by the Treatment Bookings Team, Finance Team or any other administrative employee"

column4: Treatment plan changes must be submitted through the system as an authorised Treatment Modification Request; requests made only by email, telephone or informal communication must not be processed.
column5: "Requests made only by email, telephone or informal communication must not be processed"

column4: Where treatment is urgently postponed for patient safety, the responsible clinician must subsequently record and authorise the decision retrospectively.
column5: "system must also support urgent situations... responsible clinician subsequently records and authorises the decision"

column4: Any treatment modification that affects an existing charge, funding approval or completed payment must be referred to the Finance Team for review.
column5: "Any treatment modification that affects an existing charge... must also be referred to the Finance Team"

column4: Appointments must be identified using the hospital's external scheduling service, with the result written back to the system.
column5: "identify an appropriate appointment using the hospital's external scheduling service"

column4: Patients are notified by letter; where the appointment is due to take place within the following two weeks, the patient must also be contacted by telephone.
column5: "if the appointment is due to take place within the following two weeks, the patient must also be contacted by telephone"

column4: Every contact attempt and its outcome (unanswered, incorrect number, alternative requested) must be recorded.
column5: "Each contact attempt and its outcome must be recorded"

column4: Where an external service is unavailable, the booking must remain pending, the responsible team must be notified and subsequent attempts recorded, without creating duplicate appointments.
column5: "booking must remain pending... without creating duplicate appointments"

column4: Before a treatment appointment can be confirmed, the system must determine whether the treatment is funded by the hospital, covered by an approved insurer or funding organisation, or requires payment by the patient.
column5: "system must determine whether the patient's treatment is funded by the hospital, covered by an approved insurer... or requires payment by the patient"

column4: Where funding approval is required, the Finance Team must record the responsible funding organisation, the authorisation reference, the approved amount and any limitations.
column5: "Finance Team must record the responsible funding organisation, authorisation reference, approved amount and any limitations"

column4: The system must not store the patient's complete card information or other unnecessary financial details.
column5: "must not store the patient's complete card information or other unnecessary financial details"

column4: An appointment requiring advance payment must not normally be confirmed until the payment has been successfully completed, or an authorised exemption, funding approval or payment arrangement has been recorded.
column5: "must not normally be confirmed until the payment has been successfully completed, or an authorised exemption, funding approval or payment arrangement has been recorded"

column4: Declined, cancelled, duplicated or incomplete payments must notify the patient and the responsible administrative team; a further payment attempt may be allowed but must not create a duplicate booking or charge the patient more than once.
column5: "allow another payment attempt without creating a duplicate booking or charging the patient more than once"

column4: Where the external PSP has taken payment but the confirmation was not returned because of a communication failure, the transaction must be marked for investigation rather than automatically requesting another payment.
column5: "marked for investigation rather than automatically requesting another payment"

column4: Clinical staff must still be able to authorise urgent treatment even where payment has not been confirmed; the reason must be recorded and the case referred to the Finance Team.
column5: "Clinical staff must still be able to authorise urgent treatment... reason... recorded and referred to the Finance Team"

column4: Only an authorised member of the Finance Team may determine whether a full or partial refund is appropriate; the refund instruction is sent to the external Payment Service Provider and the outcome recorded against the patient's account.
column5: "an authorised member of the Finance Team determines whether a full or partial refund is appropriate... sent to the external Payment Service Provider"

column4: Clinical staff may provide treatment information but must not approve financial refunds unless they also hold the required financial authority; members of the Finance Team must not make decisions about whether treatment is clinically necessary.
column5: "Clinical staff may provide information... but must not approve financial refunds unless they also hold the required financial authority. Similarly, members of the Finance Team must not make decisions about whether treatment is clinically necessary"

column4: The Consultant remains responsible for the clinical content of the Clinic Letter and must approve it before it can be distributed.
column5: "The Consultant remains responsible for the clinical content... must approve it before it can be distributed"

column4: Administrative staff may correct formatting and clear administrative errors but must not change the clinical meaning of a letter; suspected clinical errors must be returned to the Consultant.
column5: "Administrative staff may correct formatting and clear administrative errors but must not change the clinical meaning... returned to the Consultant"

column4: Clinic Letters must be completed, approved, processed and sent within seven days of the relevant appointment.
column5: "completed, approved, processed and sent within seven days of the relevant appointment"

column4: A letter not completed within seven days is treated as delayed; where the delay exceeds one month it must be escalated to the Administrative Manager, and where it exceeds three months it must be escalated to a higher management team.
column5: "more than seven days... delayed; more than one month... escalated to the Administrative Manager; more than three months... higher management team"

column4: The system must prevent repeated reminders once a letter has been completed, support authorised staff in recording valid reasons for delay, and retain a full history of reminders, responses and escalations.
column5: "prevent repeated reminders... support authorised staff in recording valid reasons... retain a full history"

column4: Where no follow-up appointment is available within the clinically requested period, the case must be highlighted and referred to the relevant pathway team rather than being silently booked outside that period.
column5: "case must be highlighted and referred to the relevant pathway team rather than being silently booked outside the clinically requested period"

column4: Cancellations, declines and non-attendance must be recorded, and a decision made on whether another appointment should be offered, the pathway reviewed by clinical staff, or the referrer informed; paid appointments must be referred to the Finance Team.
column5: "record these events and decide whether another appointment should be offered... If a paid appointment is cancelled... referred to the Finance Team"

column4: Call handlers may answer straightforward administrative questions, must refer payment and funding matters to the Finance Team, and must refer clinical matters to clinical staff; they must not diagnose a condition, interpret test results, recommend treatment or give clinical advice.
column5: "Call handlers may answer straightforward administrative questions... must not diagnose a condition, interpret test results, recommend treatment"

column4: Every enquiry must be recorded, classified, assigned a priority and routed to the appropriate team; urgent clinical concerns must be highlighted immediately.
column5: "Every enquiry must be recorded, classified, assigned a priority and routed... Urgent clinical concerns must be highlighted immediately"

column4: The hospital has not yet agreed a complete set of rules for determining the urgency of an enquiry (see OQ-01).
column5: "the hospital has not yet agreed a complete set of rules for determining urgency"

column4: The system must authenticate users and apply role-based access controls.
column5: "authenticate users, apply role-based access controls"

column4: Audit records must identify the user, date, time and nature of each significant action, and must not be editable by ordinary users.
column5: "Audit records must identify the user, date, time and nature of each action and must not be editable by ordinary users"

column4: The system must maintain accurate patient identification information and reduce the risk of records being associated with the wrong patient where information is received from different organisations or external services.
column5: "maintain accurate patient identification information and reduce the risk of records being associated with the wrong patient"

column4: The system must provide an appropriate procedure for recording activities completed during any period of system or external-service unavailability.
column5: "provide an appropriate procedure for recording activities completed during any period of system or external-service unavailability"
